title: Renewal Requests on Prescriptions: Class Windows, Fax Use and Frequency
content:
When a patient's prescription needs a new authorization, Kestrel sends the prescriber a renewal request. For Kestrel Prescriptions, the handling class sets whether requests are sent at all, how early a request may go while refills remain, whether fax is permitted, how long to wait before sending again, and how many requests may go in rolling 30 days.

| Handling class | Renewal requests sent | Window before the expiration date (calendar days) | Fax permitted | Resend after (business days without reply) | Most requests per prescription in rolling 30 days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Controlled Acute Prescription | Yes | 10 | Yes | 2 | 3 |
| Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription | Yes | 14 | Yes | 2 | 3 |
| Schedule V Controlled Prescription | Yes | 14 | Yes | 2 | 3 |
| Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription | Yes | 7 | No | 2 | 2 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | Yes | 7 | No | 2 | 2 |
| Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription | Yes | 21 | Yes | 1 | 3 |

## What each figure means

- **Window before the expiration date** — the calendar days before the expiration date from which a renewal request may be sent while refills remain.
- **Fax permitted** — whether a request may go by fax when the prescriber cannot receive it electronically.
- **Resend after** — the business days without a prescriber reply after which the request may be sent again.
- **Most requests in rolling 30 days** — the limit on requests per prescription in any rolling 30 days.

## Training questions

**How early may a request go on a Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription that still has refills?** From 21 calendar days before its expiration date.

**May a request for a Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription go by fax?** No; its fax column is No.

**How many requests may go on a Schedule II Controlled Prescription in rolling 30 days?** At most 2.
